memories.content: Calculate user study compensation budgets based on estimated participation burden, combining session time and preparation effort.
Compensate for required travel time in face-to-face user studies as well.
Compensate for the actual time participants spent in sessions, regardless of research modality.
Leave cash payment as an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.
If compensation equity is explained, do not require finalizing the payment method at the proposal stage.
Apply the same base hourly rate to face-to-face and remote studies if task burden is equal.
Participants judge compensation fairness based on the total burden, combining session time with required travel and preparation time.
Account in compensation for the burden of rescheduling iterations and returning for multiple formative evaluation sessions.
Compensate participants for time already invested even if a session is terminated early due to prototype errors.
The author of this proposal tends to exclude preparation burden between sessions when calculating compensation for iterative studies.
Use an em dash only for a deliberate interruption or sharp contrast; otherwise split the sentence or choose ordinary punctuation.
In procedural passages, begin each sentence with the action, condition, or output instead of repeating “we” so the steps remain easy to follow and reuse.
Write system behaviors confirmed in the actual usage environment as observed states.
Write system behaviors not yet confirmed in the field as conditional plans.
Readers can reconstruct a sequence more accurately when each sentence begins with the action or condition rather than the author.
Do not mechanically split connected thoughts into separate short sentences when doing so destroys the intended reading rhythm.
Preserve a longer sentence when its clauses form one continuous movement that is easier to follow together than apart.
The user understands that short sentences are easier to scan but feels that uniformly segmented prose loses its reading rhythm.
Write procedural sentences so their opening phrase can be reused as a checklist item without changing the step's meaning.
The user should choose “I” as an individual author or “we” for a named team and should not mix them when describing the same responsible party.
Action-first procedural sentences can be reordered or copied into a checklist more easily because their subject is the step rather than the proposal author.
The user can explain whether an em dash marks an intentional interruption or contrast rather than using it decoratively.
An em dash creates a stronger interruption than a comma and can make a deliberate contrast easier to hear in the sentence.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate domains: participant-compensation policy and procedural writing style. Neither supplies a counterpart to the other’s claims, so the ledger preserves each independently, including compensation practices that may diverge from stated burden principles.

relations.reason: These memories state or split the same reference-only burden principle and its fairness rationale; the compared frame has no compensation counterpart.
relations.summary: Compensation should reflect total participation burden, including session time, preparation, and required travel.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only rule about compensable time across modalities.
relations.summary: Actual session time should be compensated regardless of study modality.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim governs compensation method availability, not compensation amount or writing style.
relations.summary: Cash should remain an available payment method for face-to-face studies.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only rule about when payment-method selection must be finalized.
relations.summary: A proposal may leave the payment method unsettled when compensation equity is explained.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim establishes modality-neutral base-rate equity.
relations.summary: Equal task burden should receive the same base hourly rate in face-to-face and remote studies.

relations.reason: This is a reference-only policy for burdens created by iterative participation.
relations.summary: Compensation should account for rescheduling iterations and repeated formative-evaluation attendance.

relations.reason: This independent reference-only claim addresses compensation after an unsuccessful session.
relations.summary: Participants should be paid for time already invested when prototype errors terminate a session early.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided descriptive observation about current calculation practice, distinct from the reference frame’s prescriptive compensation principles.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to omit between-session preparation burden from iterative-study compensation calculations.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories state and justify one punctuation rule concerning the em dash’s deliberate rhetorical function.
relations.summary: Use an em dash only for an intentional strong interruption or contrast that can be explained as such.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories restate one action-first writing principle and its operational benefits.
relations.summary: Begin procedural sentences with the action, condition, or output so sequences remain clear, reusable, reorderable, and checklist-ready.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories split one documentation rule according to explicit confirmation status.
relations.summary: Describe field-confirmed system behavior as observed state and unconfirmed behavior as a conditional plan.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories express one preference and rationale for retaining continuous sentence movement.
relations.summary: Preserve connected thoughts in longer sentences when mechanical segmentation would damage clarity or reading rhythm.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only rule about consistent attribution of responsibility.
relations.summary: Use “I” for an individual author or “we” for a named team without mixing them for the same responsible party.

reports.compared_only: Writing guidance covers action-first procedures, evidentiary framing, sentence rhythm, em-dash discipline, checklist reuse, and consistent authorial pronouns.
reports.reference_only: Compensation guidance covers total burden, modality-neutral time and rates, travel, repeated participation, early termination, payment methods, proposal timing, and a reported tendency to omit between-session preparation.
